newsitem.title: UK: UK loses VAT test case in European court - PA.
newsitem.headline: UK loses VAT test case in European court - PA.

text.p: Britain has lost a test case on value added tax payments in the European Court of Justice, the UK Press Association reported on Thursday.
The Press Association said the UK Treasury could face losses running into billions of pounds following the case.
The PA said judges ruled that Customs and Excise levied too much tax from catalogue retailer Argos Plc on discounted promotional vouchers.
The finding paves the way for a series of similar cases, which could knock billions off Customs revenues, upsetting Government calculations of the tax take, the PA said.
The court agreed that British Customs and Excise wrongly interpreted EU VAT rules, the PA said.
The judges in the European Court of Justice upheld the claims of catalogue retailer Argos and toiletries manufacturer Elida Gibbs that too much tax was levied on special discount offers to customers.
In the case of Argos, it involved vouchers issued and sold by the company under an incentive scheme to encourage trade at its more than 300 outlets in Britain.
The vouchers could be used for part or full payment for goods or services bought in Argos showrooms, but could not be redeemed for cash.
Customs and Excise officials calculated the VAT payable by Argos on the basis of receipts from sales of goods, regardless of the discounted value of the vouchers used in some cases, the PA reported.
Accountants Coopers have suggested that final claims covering VAT's 23-year history could dwarf the National Debt.
Test cases were submitted to Luxembourg for a ruling on EU law by the VAT and Duties Tribunal, which is considering the companies' complaints, the PA said.

Today, the judges at the European Court ruled that it was the face value of the vouchers or coupons handed out or bought which was relevant for the VAT take, and not the full value of goods received in exchange, PA reported.
